chunks: And from him, from al-Abbas ibn Musa al-Warraq, from Yunus, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Raising your two hands in the prayer is its adornment.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of raising hands during prayer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes raising the hands (raf' al-yadayn) during prayer as its 'adornment' (zīnah), emphasizing the aesthetic and spiritual beauty of the ritual's physical movements. This view is particularly significant in Shia jurisprudence as it supports the practice of raising hands at the beginning of prayer and before bowing, distinguishing it from the Hanafi preference for keeping hands still, thereby highlighting the harmony between outward form and inward devotion.
